title: A Suspicious Text Message
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a young woman who received a strange text message. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a young woman received a text message on her smartphone.
scenes: コマ1:会社員の女性が電車の中でスマートフォンを見ると、「荷物を届けられませんでした。下のリンクから再配達の手続きをしてください」というメッセージが届いている。
コマ2:「The next day」。女性が職場で同僚にメッセージを見せると、同僚が「それは詐欺かもしれないよ」と指摘している。
コマ3:「A week later」。会社の会議室で、オンライン詐欺についての研修が行われ、社員たちが真剣にメモを取っている。
コマ4:「The following Sunday」。女性が実家で、父親が知らない番号からの「税金の還付金があります」という電話に、銀行の暗証番号を伝えようとしているところを慌てて止めている。
narrationSample: One day, a young woman received a text message on her smartphone saying that a package could not be delivered. It asked her to click a link to arrange redelivery. The next day, she showed the message to a coworker, who told her that it was probably a scam. A week later, her company held a seminar on online fraud, and the employees took careful notes. The following Sunday, she was visiting her father when he got a phone call about a tax refund. He was just about to give out his bank password, but she quickly stopped him and told him to hang up and check with the bank first.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the woman, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I'm glad I stopped my father in time. Scammers are getting smarter, so we should talk about these tricks with our families and always check suspicious calls with the official phone number."

questions.question: Do you think people today are well protected against online fraud?
questions.sampleAnswer: I don't think so. Many people still don't know how to recognize fake messages, and scammers now use websites and logos that look very real. Schools and companies should give regular lessons on digital safety.

questions.question: Should online platforms be held responsible for fraudulent advertisements or messages on their services?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Many scams start with social media or online ads, so platforms should check their advertisers more carefully and remove suspicious accounts quickly. However, individuals also need to be careful, because no system can catch every scam.

title: A Street Musician
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a young man who played music in front of a train station. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One evening, a young man was playing his guitar in front of a train station.
scenes: コマ1:若い男性が夕方、駅前でギターを弾きながら歌っていて、足を止めた人たちが拍手を送っている。
コマ2:「The next week」。近くのマンションの住人が、夜遅くまで続く演奏の音について市役所に苦情を伝えている。
コマ3:「A month later」。市が駅前の一角に、演奏できる時間と音量を決めた「路上演奏の専用スペース」を作り、男性がそこで演奏している。
コマ4:「That evening」。男性が、マンションの窓から自分の演奏を静かに聞いている女性に気づき、ギターを抱えて考え込んでいる。
narrationSample: One evening, a young man was playing his guitar in front of a train station, and several people stopped to listen and applaud. The next week, however, some residents of a nearby apartment building complained to the city office about the noise, which continued late into the evening. A month later, the city set up a special area in front of the station where street performers could play during designated hours and at a limited volume. The young man started performing there, and he was glad that he could keep playing his music. That evening, he noticed a woman standing by the window of the apartment building, listening quietly to his music. He held his guitar and wondered what to do next.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the young man, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "Maybe that woman is one of the people who complained. I should have apologized for playing so late. I'm glad she is listening now, and I want my music to bring people together, not divide them."

questions.question: Do you think cities should allow more street performances?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Street performances make cities more lively and give young artists a chance to show their talent. However, there should be clear rules so that performances don't disturb people who live nearby.

questions.question: Should the government spend public money to support artists?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think it should, at least partly. Many artists struggle to make a living, and if they stop creating, a country's culture becomes poorer. However, public support should focus on young artists who really need help, rather than on people who are already successful.

title: A Stargazing Club
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a high school boy who loved looking at the stars. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One night, a high school boy set up his telescope in the backyard of his house.
scenes: コマ1:高校生の男の子が自宅の庭で望遠鏡を組み立てているが、街の明かりが強くて夜空の星がほとんど見えず、がっかりしている。
コマ2:「The next month」。男の子が天文クラブの仲間と、郊外の山へ星の観察に行く計画を地図を見ながら話し合っている。
コマ3:「That weekend」。山の上で、夜空いっぱいに天の川が広がり、仲間たちが歓声を上げている。
コマ4:「A few months later」。町の商店街に巨大なネオンの看板が新しくでき、夜の街がまぶしく照らされていて、男の子が空を見上げて顔をしかめている。
narrationSample: One night, a high school boy set up his telescope in the backyard of his house, but he was disappointed because the bright city lights made it almost impossible to see the stars. The next month, he and his friends in the astronomy club planned a trip to a mountain outside the city. That weekend, they reached the top of the mountain, and the Milky Way stretched across the entire night sky. Everyone cheered with excitement. A few months later, however, a huge neon sign was installed on the shopping street, and the town became even brighter at night. The boy looked up at the sky and frowned, worried that the stars would soon disappear from his town altogether.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the boy, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "Light pollution is getting worse, and most people don't even realize how much of the night sky they are losing. Our club should write to the town council and suggest lights that don't shine upward."

questions.question: Do you think it is important to protect the night sky?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Light pollution affects not only astronomy but also animals that depend on natural light and people's sleep. Being able to see the stars also gives children a sense of wonder about science.

questions.question: Should cities limit the brightness of outdoor advertising at night?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think they should. Bright signs use a lot of electricity, which increases carbon emissions. Reasonable limits would save energy and protect the environment, although businesses should be consulted so that their advertising still works well.

title: Deer in the Town
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a farmer whose vegetable field was damaged by wild deer. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One autumn, a farmer found that his vegetable field had been damaged overnight.
scenes: コマ1:秋の朝、農家の男性が、畑の野菜が食べられて荒らされているのを見て、がっかりしている。地面にはシカの足跡が残っている。
コマ2:「The next week」。男性が市役所の担当者に相談し、山の木の実が減ったため、シカが人里に下りてくることが多くなったと説明を受けている。
コマ3:「A month later」。住民たちが畑の周りに金網の柵を立て、夜間に見回りをするボランティアを組織している。
コマ4:「That winter」。男性が柵の外で、雪の中を歩くシカの群れを見つめ、どうすれば人と動物が共存できるか考えている。
narrationSample: One autumn, a farmer found that his vegetable field had been badly damaged overnight. He saw deer footprints everywhere and was very disappointed. The next week, he consulted an official at the city office, who explained that the deer were coming down from the mountains because there were fewer acorns and other wild foods there. A month later, residents had built a wire fence around the fields and organized volunteers to patrol the area at night. The farmer was relieved that the damage had stopped. That winter, however, he stood outside the fence and watched a herd of deer walking through the snow. He wondered how people and animals could live together without harming each other.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the farmer, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "The deer are not the only problem. People have changed the mountains, so the animals are coming into towns to look for food. We need to protect our crops, but we also need to find a way to live with wildlife."

questions.question: Do you think hunting is a good way to control the number of wild animals in Japan?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think it is necessary in some cases, because the number of deer and wild boars has increased a lot. However, hunters are getting older, so the government also needs to train new hunters and find other solutions, such as better fences and careful management of food waste.

questions.question: Should farmers receive more government support to protect their crops from wild animals?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Many small farmers cannot afford high fences or electric wires on their own, and losing crops can threaten their business. Financial support would help them protect their land and keep farming alive in rural areas.

title: A Sign Language Class
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a man who started learning sign language. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a man noticed that his deaf coworker had trouble taking part in a meeting.
scenes: コマ1:会社の会議で、耳が聞こえない同僚の女性が、ほかの社員が次々に話す中、ノートに筆談で必死に意見を書こうとしている。男性社員は何もできずに申し訳なさそうにしている。
コマ2:「The next week」。男性が市民センターの掲示板で手話教室の案内を見つけ、申し込み用紙に記入している。
コマ3:「Six months later」。男性が同僚の女性と、手話を交えながら笑顔で昼食を取っている。
コマ4:「One morning」。会議の前、男性が同僚たちに簡単な手話のあいさつを一緒に覚えようと提案しているが、ほかの社員たちは戸惑った顔をしている。
narrationSample: One day, a man noticed that his deaf coworker had trouble taking part in a meeting. Everyone was speaking quickly, and she was trying hard to write her opinions in a notebook, but by then the discussion had already moved on. The man felt sorry that he could not help her. The next week, he found a notice about a sign language class at the community center and signed up. Six months later, he was having lunch with his coworker, and they were laughing together as they communicated with signs and gestures. One morning, before a meeting, he suggested that his colleagues learn a few simple signs together, but many of them looked confused and did not know how to respond.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the man, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "Learning a few signs is a small step, but it can make a big difference. I hope my colleagues will become interested, and I'll ask the company to hold a short training session for everyone."

questions.question: Do you think companies are doing enough to support employees with disabilities?
questions.sampleAnswer: I don't think they are doing enough yet. Many companies only meet the legal requirement for hiring people with disabilities. They should also improve their facilities and communication methods, such as providing sign language interpreters for important meetings.

questions.question: Should public offices and hospitals be required to provide sign language interpreters?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think they should, at least at major public offices and hospitals. Communication is a basic right, and interpreters allow people to access important information. However, the government would need to train enough interpreters, so the rule should be introduced step by step.

title: A Delayed Train
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a commuter whose train was stopped by heavy snow. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One morning, a commuter was stuck on a train that had stopped in the snow.
scenes: コマ1:雪の朝、男性会社員が停車したままの電車の車内で、腕時計を見ていらいらしている。
コマ2:「That afternoon」。駅のホームで、遅れて来た乗客たちが駅員に詰め寄り、駅員が何度も頭を下げている。
コマ3:「A month later」。鉄道会社が遅延情報をリアルタイムで知らせるアプリを導入し、男性がそのアプリで別ルートの電車を調べている。
コマ4:「The following winter」。大雪で電車が再び止まり、若い駅員が一人で、ホームに集まった大勢の乗客の質問に答えている。男性は手伝うべきか迷っている。
narrationSample: One morning, a commuter was stuck on a train that had stopped because of heavy snow. He grew more and more annoyed as he watched the minutes pass. That afternoon, after he finally reached the station, many passengers were arguing with a station attendant, who kept bowing and apologizing. A month later, the railway company introduced an app that sent real-time updates about delays. The commuter used it to check alternative routes, and he felt much less stressed. The following winter, however, another heavy snowfall stopped the trains again. He saw a young attendant trying to answer questions from a huge crowd on the platform alone, and he wondered whether he should go over and help.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the man, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "That attendant is working hard alone, and the passengers are frustrated. I could help by answering simple questions or guiding people to the bus stop, but I should be careful not to get in the way."

questions.question: Do you think people in Japan expect too much punctuality from public transportation?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think it's partly true. Punctuality is an important part of our culture, and it helps people plan their lives. However, people sometimes expect perfect service even in extreme weather, which puts a lot of pressure on station staff.

questions.question: Should railway companies be required to pay compensation to passengers when trains are delayed?
questions.sampleAnswer: I don't think companies should have to pay for every delay, because weather and accidents are beyond their control. However, if delays are caused by poor maintenance, the companies should be held responsible. Better information would help passengers more than money.
